findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the specific upstream source for the vendored GitLab CI schema (GitLab's authoritative gitlab-org CI/CD schema vs SchemaStore's community gitlab-ci.json) and state why it was chosen, so the immutable-revision + SHA-256 provenance pins against a known origin.
evidence: Plan quote: 'validated offline against a vendored Draft-07 schema with immutable upstream revision, retrieval date, dialect, and SHA-256 provenance'
Retrieved GitLab Docs: 'The CI/CD schema follows the JSON Schema Draft-07 specification' — GitLab's own schema is authoritative and Draft-07
Retrieved SchemaStore/Lintel catalog: a separate community 'gitlab-ci' JSON schema also exists (gitlab-ci.json)
ABSENCE: the plan text names neither the gitlab-org upstream nor SchemaStore, so a reader cannot tell which provenance chain the immutable revision + SHA-256 pin against
findings.finding: The plan asserts a 'vendored Draft-07 schema' for GitLab portability validation with immutable-revision + SHA-256 provenance, but does not identify which upstream source the schema comes from. Two real, distinct candidates exist with different maintenance/provenance semantics: GitLab's own gitlab-org CI/CD schema (authoritative, Draft-07 per GitLab Docs) and SchemaStore's community gitlab-ci.json. Naming the source is prior-art selection that anchors what 'immutable upstream revision' pins to.
findings.location: Context, para 4 ('GitLab portability is validated offline against a vendored Draft-07 schema with immutable upstream revision, retrieval date, dialect, and SHA-256 provenance'); AC 'GitLab schema provenance records and verifies an immutable upstream revision and checksum.'
scenarios: Author vendors the SchemaStore community copy when the authoritative gitlab-org schema was intended (or vice versa), producing a provenance pin against a source that lags or diverges from GitLab's own validation semantics
findings.suggested_fix: State in the Context/AC that the vendored schema is GitLab's authoritative gitlab-org CI/CD Draft-07 schema (per GitLab Docs 'Contribute to the CI/CD Schema'), with the pinned upstream commit/tag, retrieval date, dialect, and SHA-256 recorded; if SchemaStore's gitlab-ci.json is used instead, justify the community-source choice explicitly.
